Per the title, this is something I've been wanting to see for a long time now, but it was always filed in the back of my head to look it up another day.

Well, a couple of months ago, I finally signed up over at Spot the Station, and this morning, I got the email.

I set a reminder on my phone, and have been giddy about it all day.

Sure enough, my reminder went off, and I ran outside and looked the direction I knew it to be coming from.

Right on time, it lit up like a beacon in the sky.

Just knowing how fast it was traveling and that there are currently HUMANS in that box put me in awe about space again.

I just had to share this with someone, and to encourage any of you space-lovers that haven't taken the chance to view it, go sign up immediately.
I just watched the ISS pass almost directly overhead, and it was very humbling.
Thanks for bringing this up. The kids will get a kick out of it someday.
Questions: I live in a big city. Are the lights going to drown out what i can see? And, can you see with the naked eye?

Yes, you can see it without aids! In the city, the lights shouldn't be a problem (if you can see any stars or planets you should be able to see the ISS), but buildings might. From what I've seen it is not likely to pass directly overhead very often, so you'd need a clearing or some elevation. I just looked at the linked page, and this week is very active for my area- up to 4 visible orbits some nights lasting up to 6 minutes. I would suggest signing up for the alerts and giving it a go!

If you are looking in the North-Northwest direction, it should come into view about 11° above the horizon. They have a page with a little more info here. Happy hunting!
